title: Best Solar Generator Kits Under $500 (2026): 288 Wh or 1 kWh?
short_title: Solar generator under $500: 288 Wh or 1 kWh?
summary: What a solar generator kit under $500 actually buys, from the kits on the makers' own US stores: the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W panel (288 Wh) against the ALLPOWERS P1800 + 200 W panel (1,024 Wh), what 288 Wh runs, how long a 100 W panel takes to refill it, and the solar-voltage trap when you add a panel later.
short_summary: Under $500, a solar generator kit is either a 288 Wh station with a 100 W panel or, with a code, ALLPOWERS' 1,024 Wh P1800 with a 200 W panel.

long.say: Two kits are worth a look. The BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 with a hundred-watt panel: two hundred eighty-eight watt-hours, LiFePO4 cells and a six-hundred-watt inverter. And the ALLPOWERS P1800 with a two-hundred-watt flexible panel: one thousand twenty-four watt-hours, about three and a half times the battery, with an eighteen-hundred-watt inverter. The catch: it was a pre-order when we checked, and it gets under five hundred dollars only with its code. Today's price and status are in the description.

items: 288 Wh LiFePO4 · 600 W inverter · 100 W panel
1,024 Wh LiFePO4 · 1,800 W inverter · 200 W flexible panel

long.say: What does two hundred eighty-eight watt-hours run? About twenty to twenty-five phone charges, a fifteen-watt laptop for fifteen to eighteen hours, a forty-watt fan for six or seven hours, or a CPAP without its humidifier for one night. It won't run a fridge for long, a kettle or a heater. For those, size up to one kilowatt-hour.

How fast does the panel refill it? A hundred-watt folding panel gives about seventy-five watts in full sun, so it takes roughly four hours of full sun to refill two hundred eighty-eight watt-hours. In winter or cloud, plan on a day or more. The P1800's two-hundred-watt panel needs about seven to eight hours of full sun for its much bigger battery: one and a half to two sunny days.

slide.cap: of full sun for a 100 W panel to refill 288 Wh
slide.note: A 100 W folding panel gives about 75 W in full sun. Winter or cloud: a day or more.

long.say: Here's how they compare with the other small kits. BLUETTI's Elite 30 mini kit has a three-hundred-watt inverter, half the Elite 30 V2's. Jackery's Solar Generator 300 comes with only a forty-watt panel. And Anker's C300X DC kit has no AC outlets at all, just DC and USB. EcoFlow's RIVER 3 Plus is a good station, but its US store sells no bundle, so under five hundred means buying two separate items.

slide.foot: Specs from each maker's US page, read 2026-11-02

long.say: One trap if you plan to add a panel later. The Elite 30 V2's solar input takes twelve to twenty-eight volts and two hundred watts at most, so the big folding panels, at forty volts or more, are too high-voltage for it. The P1800 takes eleven to sixty volts and up to six hundred fifty watts, so it has room to grow.
